title: Agentic Engineering Patterns: AI Should Help Us Produce Better Code
description: Simon Willison argues that AI coding agents should help produce better code, not worse. He addresses developer concerns that outsourcing code to AI tools will result in quality degradation. His key insight: if adopting coding agents reduces code quality, that's a fixable process issue, not an inevitable outcome. Shipping worse code with agents is a choice, and we can choose to ship better code instead. This is part of his broader 'Agentic Engineering Patterns' project documenting best practices for AI-assisted development.
author: Simon Willison

title: Andrej Karpathy Predicts 2026 Will Be the 'Slopacolypse'
description: According to Reddit discussions of his tweets, Andrej Karpathy predicts that 2026 will be the 'Slopacolypse' - suggesting AI will be writing most code, potentially leading to concerns about code quality or over-reliance on AI-generated code. He notes how hard it is to communicate how much programming has changed due to AI in recent months, mentioning that AI is suddenly writing most of his code, leading to concerns about atrophying his ability to write code manually.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: Hacker News: Are LLM Merge Rates Not Getting Better?
description: A Hacker News discussion from March 2026 with 149 comments discussing LLM performance and improvements over time. The conversation explores whether merge rates (a key metric for LLM code generation quality) are improving and what this means for the state of AI coding tools. This reflects ongoing technical debates in the developer community about LLM progress.
